description: Self-test for the diagnostic `message` opt-in (issue #1025). A fixture opts into having its learner prose compared by carrying a `message` key at all; before #1025 the harness dropped `message` unconditionally, so 306 of the corpus's 632 diagnostic objects asserted prose that nothing read -- and a producer emitting the wrong sentence for `ol-reserved-word` survived the whole corpus. This fixture proves the opt-in has teeth. Every other field -- `code`, `source_span` (document, start and end), `params`, `stage`, `severity` -- is identical to what `check()` actually produces for `define forward :n`, so the ONLY thing that can make the harness report a mismatch is the message, and `expect: "mismatch"` turns that detection into a pass. The wrong sentence used here is not invented: it is issues #751 and #871 verbatim, which shipped twice and leaked the word *primitive* at a learner -- `spec/error-model.md:125` makes *keyword*, *primitive* and *alias* a MUST NOT in this message, and a MUST NOT about message text is unenforceable by a harness that never reads message text. The run log prints this self-test's own report, which names `message` as the sole differing field. The opposite arm -- a diagnostic with NO `message` key still passing while prose differs, which no fixture can express, since it would have to record the prose it is not asserting -- is pinned as a unit test on `compare()` in scripts/conformance.test.mjs.

diagnostics.message: forward is already a reserved primitive, so it can't be redefined here.
